openSourceAccessibility.meta.title: Local Speech Input for Accessibility – TypeWhisper
openSourceAccessibility.meta.description: TypeWhisper opens selected building blocks for local speech input, assistive text workflows, and more accessible digital work.
openSourceAccessibility.hero.title: Local speech input for more accessible digital work.
openSourceAccessibility.hero.subtitle: TypeWhisper is opening selected building blocks for local speech input, assistive text workflows, and more accessible digital work. The goal is a reusable open-source core for people who cannot type continuously, quickly, or without pain – local, documented, and independent from any single cloud service.

openSourceAccessibility.problem.title: The access gap is practical.
openSourceAccessibility.problem.descript: Many digital tools still assume that people can type quickly, use a mouse precisely, and recover from repetitive input without pain. That leaves out people with motor limitations, chronic pain, fatigue, tremor, visual strain, dyslexia, temporary injuries, and many everyday work contexts where typing is the wrong interface.
openSourceAccessibility.approach.title: Start from local, user-controlled speech.
openSourceAccessibility.approach.descrip: The initiative builds on TypeWhisper surfaces that already matter for accessibility: system-wide dictation, file transcription, assistive text workflows, local engines, plugin extension points, an HTTP API, and a CLI. The goal is not a separate grant-only product, but reusable pieces that make local speech input easier to inspect, adapt, and deploy.
openSourceAccessibility.principles.title: Principles of the initiative
openSourceAccessibility.principles.subti: Funding can help the work move faster, but it should not change the trust model that makes TypeWhisper useful.
Speech and text workflows should be usable without forcing audio or drafts through a remote service.
openSourceAccessibility.principle.assist: The work should cover dictation, correction, rewriting, snippets, and repeatable text actions across normal desktop tools.
openSourceAccessibility.principle.open.d: Reusable docs, examples, integration patterns, and technical building blocks should be public when they can help others.
openSourceAccessibility.principle.honest: No paid recommendations, no hidden placements, no in-app advertising, and no licensing rights through funding.
openSourceAccessibility.blocks.title: What should become open.
openSourceAccessibility.blocks.subtitle: The plan is to produce reusable public building blocks that can be used independently from the commercial TypeWhisper product.
openSourceAccessibility.block.speech.des: Guides and integration examples for local speech engines, privacy-preserving transcription, and user-controlled engine selection.
Reusable templates for cleaning up dictated text, transforming selected text, and reducing repetitive typing.
openSourceAccessibility.block.integratio: Technical examples for CLI, local API, plugins, and organizational deployment patterns.
openSourceAccessibility.block.guides.des: Material for workplace, education, and advisory settings, privacy review, accessibility testing, and pilot projects.
openSourceAccessibility.impact.title: How impact should become visible
openSourceAccessibility.impact.subtitle: In pilot projects, we can measure together which building blocks actually help in daily work and where barriers remain.

openSourceAccessibility.audience.title: Who it should help.
openSourceAccessibility.audience.subtitl: The initiative is aimed at three groups that need speech input to be adaptable, inspectable, and privacy-aware.
openSourceAccessibility.audience.users: Users: people who cannot type well because of motor limitations, pain, fatigue, tremor, dyslexia, visual impairment, or temporary injury.
openSourceAccessibility.audience.organiz: Organizations: advisory centers, education providers, employers, inclusion projects, and nonprofit operators.
openSourceAccessibility.audience.builder: Developers: teams that want to reuse local speech input, workflows, plugins, or accessible text automation.
openSourceAccessibility.partners.title: Partners we want to talk to.
openSourceAccessibility.partners.subtitl: The useful first step is a concrete pilot or funding conversation, not a broad logo exchange.
openSourceAccessibility.status.title: Project status
openSourceAccessibility.status.available: System-wide dictation, workflows, local engines, plugin extension points, HTTP API, and CLI.
openSourceAccessibility.status.planned.d: Documentation, example workflows, integration guides, test material, and selected technical interfaces.
openSourceAccessibility.status.wanted.de: Pilot partners, funding partners, accessibility feedback, nonprofit operators, employers, and research partners.
openSourceAccessibility.legalNote: The initiative describes planned and partly existing open-source and accessibility building blocks. TypeWhisper does not replace medical advice and is not positioned as a medical device.

openSourceAccessibility.cta.subtitle: Send a short note about the people you support, the workflow you want to improve, and whether you are thinking about funding, a pilot, or technical collaboration.
